name: Dashulya-coder/AlertForecast
type: repo (student / cohort peer project, same course)
year: 2026 (created 2026-10-12, last push 2026-10-12 20:54 UTC, at the 12 Oct deadline; 17 commits)
peer_review_status: student repo, self-reported results; not peer reviewed
target_type: State label ('an alert is active at any moment in (t, t+h]'), reported in two views: (a) all origins, which the author calls inflated by ongoing alerts; (b) 'Kyiv clear at t' in the real-time state, which is the headline. Because clear-at-t is defined in the real-time state, view (b) works out to an onset target, which is directly comparable to ours.
target_definition: y(t) = 1 if Kyiv City has an alert active at any moment in (t, t+h], half-open alerts [start, end), and an alert starting exactly at t+h counts. Origins every 30 minutes (UTC). Horizons h in {1, 3, 6} hours, one model per horizon. Headline = view (b), origins where Kyiv is clear at t as known at t.
spatial_unit: city: Kyiv City only (not Kyivska oblast). Other oblasts are used only as candidate neighbour features.
at_risk_masking: Partly. Rows are not dropped from training (the GBM is fit on all purged rows, both views), but scoring is reported separately on the clear-at-t subset, and that subset is the headline. The logistic baseline is fit on clear-at-t rows only. 'Clear' uses the real-time state, in which a naive alert stays open until the next activation, so the 'naive shadow' does not count as clear.
data_sources: Vadimkin/ukrainian-air-raid-sirens-dataset, volunteer file volunteer_data_en.csv (eTryvoga Telegram channel), snapshot 2026-10-12 05:05 UTC. Train 2022-03 to 2026-08-16, validation 2026-08-17..09-13, test 2026-09-14..10-11 (28 days, Kyiv-local days). The official file was rejected because it stops 2026-09-07 and has a feed failure from 30 Aug to 1 Sep. The alerts.in.ua API cross-check was deferred and never done.
data_source_variant: volunteer file (NOT official, NOT API); oblast-level only (the volunteer file has no raion/hromada level, so no admin-level union). Snapshot 2026-10-12 05:05 UTC. The author measured large disagreement between sources over 28 days (2026-08-09..09-06): only 32% of alert-minutes overlap, and about 20% of 30-min origins get a different label, partly because of the official outage.
preprocessing: Two interval tables: Intervals.for_region (dataset ends, labels only) and Intervals.for_region_state (real-time view: a naive alert stays open until the region's next activation; features and clear-at-t state). Overlapping intervals are merged. Completeness cutoff: the file writes only closed alerts, so Kyiv is complete only until 2026-10-11 22:10:32 UTC (derived from the last naive row plus 3h). Test origins whose label window crosses it are dropped (0/3/9 at 1h/3h/6h). The author noted that about 45% of the official file's Kyiv rows are exact duplicates, but there is no explicit dedup step in the src code for the volunteer file [uncertain]. No gap masking was needed for the volunteer file, and none was implemented. Standing alerts are not handled; this matters less for Kyiv City.
known_label_artefacts: (1) Naive / 30-min ends: the main finding. The volunteer processor (volunteer_etryvoga_processor.py) writes naive=True with end = start + 30 min ONLY when the region's next activation comes more than 3h later. A next activation within 3h overwrites the open alert. Check: 0 of 5,828 naive alerts have a next start within 3h (minimum gap exactly 3.000h), against 45.6% of non-naive alerts; only 43 of 110,340 non-naive alerts last exactly 1800s. So a 30-min duration leaks 'no alert for >= 3h'. Fix: features and clear-at-t state use the real-time view; dataset ends are used for labels only; naive, dataset durations and dataset ends are banned as features. Effect: validation persistence PR-AUC at 1h fell from 0.55 to 0.31, and the neighbour-region lift fell from up to 3.1x to 1.9-2.3x. The naive share rose from 6% in train to 28% of test alerts. A sensitivity run that excludes origins touching naive alerts leaves the conclusion unchanged. (2) Late starts: when an open alert is overwritten by a new activation within 3h, the earlier start is lost, so start times can be late. Acknowledged, not fixed. (3) Missing open alerts at the snapshot: handled with the completeness cutoff. (4) Official-file gap (30 Aug to 1 Sep) and duplicates: avoided by not using the official file. (5) Standing alerts / admin reform: not addressed (volunteer file is oblast-level).
model_family: scikit-learn HistGradientBoostingClassifier, fixed hyperparameters (no tuning, no random early stopping), one model per horizon. Baselines: persistence, hour climatology, hour x weekday climatology, a 'recent activity' logistic regression (frac_alert_24h, log1p(n_starts_24h)), and a diagnostic constant set to the evaluation window's own rate. No calibrator adopted.
features: All from the real-time state, clipped at t: Kyiv-local hour and weekday; alert open at t and open age; time since last start and last end; alert counts over 1/3/6/24h; share of time under alert over 6/24h. Rejected after pre-registered tests: recent-rate features (neutral), recency weighting (significantly worse log loss), neighbour-region alerts (Stage C: a hint at 1h only, within noise; the lift was 1.9-2.3x for Volynska, Rivnenska, Cherkaska, Zhytomyrska; Kyivska oblast lift was 0.83; national count gave no lift until 11+ regions were active). No external features (Telegram and news were skipped).
external_feature_timing: Not applicable: no external features used (Telegram/news phase skipped and listed as a limitation).
ablation_design: Yes, and it is strong. Each feature or recipe change (Stage A recency weighting and recent-rate group, 8 configs; Stage B calibrators; Stage C neighbours; final GBM vs logistic) is compared on the same three 28-day windows (val 2026-08-17..09-13, w1 07-20..08-16, w2 06-22..07-19), each fit strictly before the window with the same purge, using paired multi-window day-block bootstrap CIs. Adoption rules were written into CLAUDE.md before running and applied as written.
split_scheme: Chronological, Kyiv-local days. Train before 2026-08-17; validation 2026-08-17..09-13; test 2026-09-14..10-11. Method selection on three rolling 28-day windows (val, w1, w2), each refit before the window. For the test: refit on train+val (strict purge), no refit during the 28 test days. Strict per-horizon purge: a fit row is kept only if t + h < the first evaluation origin. Test lock: allow_test=True flag plus a marker file (.test_run_done) that refuses a second run.
metrics: PR-AUC (with base rate), Brier, Brier skill score vs climatology, log loss, precision/recall at frozen thresholds (recall targets 0.5/0.8/0.9, thresholds from pooled out-of-time predictions of the 3 blocks before the window), reliability curves, weekly calibration drift (mean prediction / observed rate). No ROC-AUC.
unit_of_metric: single unit (Kyiv City), so pooled = within-unit; no cross-unit aggregation.
baseline_strength: Persistence (real-time state), hour climatology, hour x weekday climatology, recent-activity logistic (24h activity), and a non-deployable constant at the test rate. No rolling recent-rate or calibrated-persistence baseline in our sense; the recent-activity logistic is the closest to our recent-rate bar. Test result (view b): the GBM beats climatology on Brier (1h -0.014 [-0.028, -0.004], 3h -0.079, 6h -0.146; significant) but NOT on PR-AUC. Not significantly different from the logistic baseline at any horizon. Significantly worse than a constant at the test rate (Brier +0.013 / +0.071 / +0.105). On validation the recent-activity logistic already had the best Brier among baselines.
calibration: Reliability curves on the test (figure reports/figures/test_reliability.png) in both views. Calibration candidates (none, intercept shift, Platt, Platt with recency weights 1/0.5/0.25; isotonic excluded on purpose for about 4,000 clustered rows) fitted on pooled out-of-time predictions from K=3 28-day blocks before each window. None qualified under the pre-registered rule; intercept shift was a near miss (better at 3h/6h, worse at 1h). The final model is uncalibrated.
calibration_under_drift: Explicitly measured. Weekly calibration-in-the-large on the test: mean prediction / observed rate 0.55-0.88 at 1h, 0.53-0.80 at 3h, 0.59-0.78 at 6h, so the model under-predicts in every test week. Base rate shifted from 1.5 Kyiv alerts/day (train) to 4.5 (val) and 4.6 (test). On validation the base model was at 0.63-0.67, and recency weighting made it worse (0.38-0.55) because it followed the quieter pre-surge regime. Frozen thresholds also failed to transfer: achieved recall was 0.89-0.99 against targets 0.8/0.9.
uncertainty_of_gain: Yes: day-block bootstrap (1,000 resamples for the test; 300 resamples, seed 0, for multi-window selection), 95% CIs on metrics and on paired differences (GBM minus climatology, logistic, constant). No DM test. The author notes that days are treated as independent blocks.
regime_coverage: Test 2026-09-14..10-11 lies entirely in the post-7-Sep-2026 period (after the official file froze), as seen by the volunteer/eTryvoga feed. The README does not discuss the yellow/red reform as such [uncertain]. Training spans 2022-03 to 2026-08 and so includes the Jan-2025 drone surge and the 2025 admin reform, but these are not analysed separately (oblast-level volunteer data). The main regime discussed is the Aug-Sep 2026 surge: alert frequency tripled compared with the training average.
leakage_handling: Among the strongest in the cohort. (1) Found and documented the naive 30-min end leak with data and source-code evidence, and removed it with a real-time state view. (2) Perturb-the-future tests: features and state at every t <= cutoff must be identical after truncating, or after rewriting all intervals after a cutoff that falls inside a running alert, with dense and sparse seeds. (3) Negative controls / teeth: test_perturbation_has_teeth shows the same perturbation changes labels near the cutoff. test_naive_alert_features_cannot_reveal_the_next_gap shows the dataset-ends view DOES differ (the planted leak is caught) while the real-time view does not. Neighbour features have the same tests. (4) Strict per-horizon purge, tested at the boundary row (test_boundary_row_would_leak_and_is_excluded) and checking that fit labels do not depend on the evaluation period. (5) Calibration origins never see the window (tested). (6) Climatology uses training rows only (tested). (7) Completeness cutoff for alerts still open at snapshot time. Missed or limits: labels still use imputed naive ends (noisy); late starts after overwrite are not recoverable; there is no dedup step for the volunteer file [uncertain].
test_window_hygiene: Very good. Test split locked in code (allow_test flag); a marker file stops a second run; a validation dry run of the full test script was done first. Rules for every choice (Stages A-C and final model GBM vs logistic) were pre-registered in CLAUDE.md before running and applied as written, including a rule set by the user before the run. Test evaluated once. Provenance: commit 15b25a3 plus uncommitted changes, recorded with a code hash in reports/.test_run_done, which the author admits is weak provenance. Several corrections are logged in CLAUDE.md (for example the completeness claim and the base rates redone after the naive fix).
headline_results: A null result, reported honestly. Test view (b), Kyiv clear at t, n=776/776/770: GBM PR-AUC 0.232 [0.170, 0.311] vs base rate 0.227 (1h); 0.551 vs 0.553 (3h); 0.784 vs 0.791 (6h). So there is no ranking skill above the base rate. Brier 0.188/0.318/0.270, better than climatology (significant) but worse than a constant at the test rate (0.175/0.247/0.165). GBM vs logistic baseline: no significant difference. Precision at frozen recall-0.8 thresholds is within 0.007 of the base rate. View (a), all origins: PR-AUC 0.555/0.667/0.845 vs base 0.284/0.576/0.807 and persistence 0.327/0.590/0.817; most of the gain comes from knowing an alert is open. Validation persistence PR-AUC at 1h was inflated from 0.31 to 0.55 by the naive leak before the fix. Naive-excluded sensitivity: 1h PR-AUC 0.191 vs base 0.185; conclusion unchanged.
code_available: Yes: public GitHub repo, Python package src/alertforecast + scripts per phase + pytest suite (about 50 tests) + report CSVs and figures. Data not committed (gitignored; needs the specific 2026-10-12 05:05 UTC upstream commit of volunteer_data_en.csv). No license. Pet project finished at the deadline; not maintained afterwards [uncertain].
takeaways_for_project: (1) The naive / 30-min end artefact is a LEAK in the volunteer file, not just noise: the 30-min end is written only when no new alert follows within 3h. We use the official file and KEEP the 38 exactly-30-minute durations (D-010). We should state in the README that the official file is a different channel (the leak mechanism is the volunteer processor's), and ideally run a quick check of the same signature on the official data: next-start gap after a 30-min alert, minimum gap, against the other alerts. If the official 30-min alerts also never have a next start within some window, then minutes_since_last_end can leak through them and D-010 should be revisited (needs the human's approval). (2) Persistence inflated by state leakage: their validation persistence PR-AUC went from 0.55 to 0.31 once the leak was removed. This supports our onset target + at-risk masking and our D-020 causal 24h cap (also a 'what is known at t' state rule). (3) Their perturb-the-future test with a cutoff placed INSIDE a running alert, plus a 'has teeth' check, is a good model for our tests/test_leakage.py negative control (CLAUDE.md requires one). Adopt the 'cutoff inside a running alert' case explicitly. (4) Under-prediction in every test week, after a base-rate tripling, is likely in our new-regime check (D-015 (b)/(c)). Their result supports our rolling recent-rate as the main bar (D-021), and supports reporting calibration-in-the-large per group. (5) Their logistic on 24h activity equalled the GBM: we should expect that the recent-rate baseline may not be beaten (a valid result under our rules). (6) Pre-registered adoption rules with paired block-bootstrap CIs across several windows are a cheap way to make ablations honest; this matches our D-013 week-block bootstrap. (7) The completeness cutoff (closed alerts only) matters for the D-027 API merge rule and M6: open alerts must be kept or the end of the window treated as incomplete.
best_practices: Adopt: a real-time state view separate from the label view (features never read dataset end times that are not yet observed at t); perturb-the-future tests with dense and sparse seeds and a cutoff inside an open alert; negative controls that prove the test catches a planted leak; strict per-horizon purge with a boundary-row test; a code-level test lock plus a one-shot marker file; pre-registered decision rules written before running; selection on several windows from different regimes, not one validation slice; paired day/week-block bootstrap CIs on differences; weekly calibration-in-the-large drift plots; a non-deployable 'constant at the test rate' diagnostic to show how much of the Brier score is level error; reporting the null result plainly; a completeness cutoff for snapshot data. Anti-patterns or weaknesses to avoid: a state label with an all-origins view (inflated; the author reports it only as secondary); thresholds frozen from quieter periods (did not transfer); a single unit (Kyiv only), so wide CIs and no cross-unit pooling; a test run on a commit plus uncommitted changes (weak provenance); depending on a volunteer source with an imputed-end artefact; no ROC-AUC reported.
